Maintenance Report — MNT-0057-005

Asset: WELL-0057 (SW-24 Well 057, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 19 Aug 2023 08:00 · Finished: 29 Aug 2023 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 250 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0057-0044 on 2023-08-17 Report written: 31 Aug 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid was weeping from the stuffing box around the polished rod. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0057-0044 showed the wellhead at 32.6 °C with the air at 30.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Packing wear sped up by a slightly misaligned polished rod.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0057-008

Asset: WELL-0057 (SW-24 Well 057, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 24 Nov 2023 08:00 · Finished: 29 Nov 2023 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 133 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0057-0058 on 2023-11-23 Report written: 30 Nov 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0057-0058 showed the wellhead at 13.5 °C with the air at 12.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 4 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Notes and recommendations

  • Clean the motor cooling fins at each scheduled service.
  • Summer heat raises the risk of motor trips on this field.

maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0057-017

Asset: WELL-0057 (SW-24 Well 057, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 18 Apr 2025 08:00 · Finished: 29 Apr 2025 13:00 · Well stopped for this job: 269 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0057-0127 on 2025-04-17 Report written: 29 Apr 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0057-0127 showed the wellhead at 28.6 °C with the air at 25.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 285 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 228 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0057-017 (WS-06).

  • Consider corrosion inhibitor injection.

maintenance.action: Fished and replaced parted rod section
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0057-023

Asset: WELL-0057 (SW-24 Well 057, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: rod string Work started: 12 Apr 2026 08:00 · Finished: 06 May 2026 19:00 · Well stopped for this job: 587 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0057-0178 on 2026-04-09 Report written: 06 May 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator noticed the pump jack running unusually light and no fluid reaching the flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0057-0178 showed the wellhead at 24.1 °C with the air at 22.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 22 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.
